correctness.rationale: For viewing axis v with v_z>0, projection of both apices into the projected equatorial triangle is equivalent to -α≤n_i·u≤β (i=1,2,3), where u=v_horizontal/v_z, α=1/(2a), β=1/(2b). The feasible polygon is a triangle when α≥2β or β≥2α, and a hexagon otherwise. The uniform hemispherical slope density (2π)^{-1}(1+||u||²)^{-3/2} and spherical exterior Gauss–Bonnet give all three quoted arccos branches. For fixed s=a+b, triangular feasible sets increase toward the hexagon and in the hexagon branch c_s(ab)=(1+2ab)/sqrt(1+4s²-8ab+16a²b²) has positive derivative for ab≤s²/4, forcing unique a=b; differentiating gives positive quadratic coefficient. Independent radial angular midpoint quadrature of the feasible slope domain agrees with analytic probabilities on five asymmetric/symmetric test pairs within 3e-7. Boundaries agree and degeneracies are Haar-null. This does not prove a full polygon-count distribution.
residual_risks: Numerical quadrature corroborates but Gauss–Bonnet and geometric reduction provide the all-direction proof.
